Use the provisional targets in Section 3 until validated. scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

Reuse portable GPUI facilities where suitable rather than wrapping the entire toolkit in a new framework. Test interface contracts with fakes and actual adapters; do not duplicate the product's business logic for each OS.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

requirement_text: Implement protected credential and application-data adapters per published OS. Use Windows Credential Manager or equivalent on Windows, the platform keychain on macOS, and a documented supported secure credential service on Linux. Store only credential references in SQLite; never fall back silently to plaintext tokens when a store is unavailable or locked. Preserve offline cached access while affected network work is held. Use appropriate per-user data/config/cache locations, stable app identity and relative managed asset paths rather than Windows-specific absolute paths. Test filesystem permissions, file locking, SQLite WAL/FTS availability, path/Unicode handling, and stable location across upgrades. Credentials and caches are per-device; this does not add cross-device synchronization. [S36]

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

Define supported desktop behavior explicitly before publishing, preserving the persistent feed and correct Open behavior. A toolkit method or Windows test does not prove another OS's integration. Closing/quit must preserve drafts, workspace, Outbox and credentials according to the shared lifecycle contract. [S33] [S35]

requirement_text: Use a personal access token as the confirmed first-release authentication path. Prefer a fine-grained PAT when all required endpoints and organization policy support it; support an organization-approved classic PAT when endpoint coverage or organization compatibility requires that alternative. Do not switch to OAuth or device authorization as an unrequested first-release dependency. A fine-grained token can be limited to one resource owner and selected repositories, so credential profiles must route appropriate PATs for different selected owners without sending an unrelated token. [S20]

requirement_text: For organizations using SAML SSO, account for the distinction between token creation, SSO authorization, and organization approval. Fine-grained tokens receive SSO authorization during creation; classic tokens require separate SSO authorization. Fine-grained tokens may also require an organization owner's approval before private resources are accessible. [S21] [S22]

Interpret `X-GitHub-SSO` when present, including partial results. A 403 or 404 caused by authorization MUST NOT be treated automatically as resource deletion. [S21]

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Authorization repair restores the same identity in 03; reconnect signals in 05 and automatic eligible outbox resumption across all writers in 07-09.
requirement_text: Provide a user-initiated action to open an appropriate GitHub PAT or SSO authorization page in the external default browser. Validate returned authorization URLs before opening them. Preserve the current screen, cached content, drafts, outbox, and synchronization checkpoints while authorization is repaired. After verifying that a replacement PAT belongs to the same GitHub user and restores the required access, reuse the existing account/resource identities and progress, retry eligible reads, and automatically resume eligible submitted actions under the persisted pause/offline settings. A different user must receive a separate account context; replacing a token must not create a new cache for the same user.

Persist only credential references in SQLite. Normal window close or application exit retains the protected token so the next launch can resume without re-entry while it remains valid. Explicit sign-out follows AUTH-11 and clears the relevant local credential material. Never include tokens in logs, URLs, diagnostics, exports, or source control.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Signed-out credential/dispatch holds begin in 03; readable local-profile UI in 04 and all-writer PAT repair in 09; complete private-data retention and in-flight lifecycle matrix in 12.
requirement_text: Explicit sign-out MUST durably mark the affected account profile as signed out, prevent new network dispatch under that profile, and remove or invalidate its locally stored PAT material. Preserve readable private cached content, drafts, saved workspace, settings, synchronization checkpoints, activity baselines, and outbox records on the PC. Users may reopen that signed-out local profile for offline work without a renewed login; show its signed-out status and hold its remote actions until a PAT for the same verified user restores access. Keep that hold across restart. Ordinary exit is not sign-out. Expired or revoked PATs likewise preserve offline use and progress while holding affected remote work. A sign-out during an in-flight mutation does not prove remote cancellation; retain its evidence for reconciliation after access is restored. Do not expose one profile's data through a different active account or assume sign-out revokes the PAT at GitHub.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Count component and shared query totals in 04; requested-review metadata in 06 and actual pending states in 07-09. Full AC-81 validates all supported writers, scope/coverage, circular styling and zero suppression in 09.
requirement_text: Review requested, Assigned to me, and Outbox MUST show a positive total in a right-aligned dark blue filled circular badge with centered white digits. Use a suitable accessible color, provisionally #173E70, and preserve a true circle, label clearance, and legibility for multi-digit totals and high-DPI scaling. A known zero draws neither a circle nor a number. Counts are totals for the current account and each view's stated repository/filter scope, not unread-notification counts or just the visible page length. Count distinct matching items for saved views. Use a trustworthy complete-query total when available; otherwise label the cached/known count and incomplete coverage, without presenting unknown or partial coverage as a confirmed empty result. Outbox counts all unresolved submitted actions, including paused, blocked, and outcome-unknown actions, and excludes drafts, download jobs, and confirmed/cancelled history. Refresh counts from shared state after ingestion, edits, scope changes, enqueue, cancellation, and confirmation without per-pane polling. Accessible names and count details must expose scope, freshness, and any coverage limitation.

requirement_text: Persist view state independently for every tab instance: selected subview, selected file or commit, diff display mode, scroll anchors, expanded discussion or diff regions, and relevant navigation history. For a PR review tab also retain its context mode, selected verified linked issue, context/code proportions, collapsed/focused surface, and separate context scroll anchors. requirement_text: Bind comments, issue edits, review submission, approvals, and merges to the originating tab's account, repository, item, and relevant revision. Changing focus while an operation is pending MUST NOT retarget it. Global navigation shortcuts apply to the focused pane; controls inside a pane apply to that pane's displayed item. Show the target repository and item in write confirmations where needed to avoid ambiguous actions.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Draft ownership primitives in 02 and local editors in 04; integrate shared pending issue/comment, review and merge operations in 07-09.
requirement_text: Multiple views of the same resource MUST share cached domain data, operation outcomes, and persistent draft identities. Reopening the same compose or review draft must reuse its draft ID. Use one active editor per draft by default; other views show the current draft preview and a Focus editor action. Do not allow independent unsynchronized copies to overwrite the same draft or submit the same pending operation twice. Separate intentional drafts remain separate records.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Restore local workspace/drafts before networking in 04; integrate all views and writers as built. Final normal-exit, signed-out, expired-PAT and delayed-network restoration closes in 12. View restoration never submits drafts.
requirement_text: Save and restore the workspace per account, including pane order and proportions, open tab order, active tabs, focused pane, per-tab view state, scroll position or anchors, navigation context, and draft references. Normal exit MUST retain this state. On restart, render cached visible content before waiting for any API response or renewed login; then start eligible background work through the shared scheduler. Load inactive tabs lazily and expose missing or inaccessible content without discarding its navigation target. Restoring a workspace MUST NOT submit unsubmitted drafts, create duplicate operations, or expose another account's private tabs. The independent outbox worker resumes already submitted eligible actions under OUTBOX-04 and the restored authentication/pause settings; view restoration is not a dispatch trigger.
evidence: Native Windows E2E-003 confirmed cached offline restore with the original two panes and exact draft after process restart. docs/reports/sprint-04.md

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Persist closing-tab state in 04; prove pending issue/review/merge operations survive view closure.
requirement_text: Closing a tab or pane MUST preserve its saved drafts, cached content, and already submitted operation tracking. Persist editor changes before closing; if that fails, keep the editor recoverable and explain the failure. Closing a pane closes its tab views and focuses a remaining pane; closing the final tab leaves a usable empty pane. Discarding a draft is a separate explicit action. Reopening a closed tab restores its saved view state when available.
evidence: Native Windows E2E-003 confirmed cached offline restore with the original two panes and exact draft after process restart. docs/reports/sprint-04.md

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

requirement_text: Share request scheduling and deduplicate in-flight fetches across views of the same resource and revision. Opening additional panes MUST NOT create independent polling loops or duplicate alerts for that resource. Give visible tabs priority within the existing schedule and rate-limit budget. Inactive tabs must not retain every large diff or continuously redraw; evict reconstructible rendering state while preserving navigation state and drafts. Closing one view must not cancel work still needed by another view or the shared write journal.
evidence: Durable policy, SQLite scheduler, real update feeds and native Windows control evidence. docs/reports/sprint-05.md

requirement_text: Repository lists, search results, in-app links, and notification activation MUST route through the workspace's open-item behavior. For notification or external URL activation, prefer a matching tab in the focused pane, otherwise the most recently active matching tab elsewhere, otherwise a new tab in the focused pane. Apply WORKSPACE-03 when choosing among matches within a pane. Navigate only the chosen tab to the requested comment or diff location. Other panes retain their positions and unsent input.

A new reachable result wakes the dispatcher once; many panes or queued items must not each probe or drain independently. Work offline disables probes and sends until explicitly turned off.

requirement_text: Keep unsubmitted drafts separate from submitted operations. Model submitted operations using queued, validating, sending, outcome unknown, waiting for remote completion, blocked/needs attention, confirmed, and cancelled states as defined in OUTBOX-02. Persist intent before delivery; show pending local changes distinctly until GitHub confirms them. Share operation state and server results across all views, independently of the originating tab's lifetime.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Local drafts/outbox persistence first; automatic replay, cancellation, preflight and uncertain-outcome handling expand from issues/comments in 07 to reviews/merges in 08-09.
requirement_text: Save a draft snapshot and durably enqueue the user's explicit submission before attempting a request. Preserve them after authorization errors, validation failures, offline transitions, server errors, and closing their tab. Enforce shared draft ownership and one operation identity across panes. Merely saving, editing, or reopening an unsubmitted draft MUST NOT enqueue it. Submitted eligible actions MUST resume automatically after restart or reconnection without asking the user to submit them again, subject to the outbox rules.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Local drafts/outbox persistence first; automatic replay, cancellation, preflight and uncertain-outcome handling expand from issues/comments in 07 to reviews/merges in 08-09.
requirement_text: A timed-out issue, comment, review, or merge operation may have succeeded remotely. Keep the submitted operation in the outbox and automatically reconcile reliable identities or server state before considering another attempt. Retry automatically only when the action is known not to have been applied or the provider has a verified safe idempotency mechanism. If the result remains ambiguous, show Outcome unknown and allow inspection or stopping further attempts without claiming remote undo. Do not blindly replay a non-idempotent request; matching text alone is not proof of success. A deliberate retry of an unresolved action must explain the possible duplicate and cannot be triggered by reconnection alone.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Local drafts/outbox persistence first; automatic replay, cancellation, preflight and uncertain-outcome handling expand from issues/comments in 07 to reviews/merges in 08-09.
requirement_text: Preserve concurrent remote edits, submitted intent, and local input. Revalidate affected fields, permissions, and revisions immediately before dispatch, including automatic replay; explain conflicts and keep the action visible as Needs attention. Retain the draft for correction. Document unavoidable races where GitHub supplies no atomic conditional operation. A temporary connectivity interruption alone must not require resubmission of an already queued action.

requirement_text: Users MUST be able to request an eligible merge while offline using a locally cached target PR, intended head commit, and chosen supported method. Durably queue that intent. Actual merge execution requires connectivity and fresh checks of PR state, permissions, allowed methods, and server requirements. A cached green check or connection indicator is not authoritative. Send the originally intended expected head commit identity; never silently substitute the current head. [S10]

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Implement and verify in the initial owning phase; repeat applicable behavior with actual evidence on each later released platform.
requirement_text: Offer merge, squash, or rebase only when supported and permitted. Respect required checks, reviews, and branch rules. Never silently use administrative bypasses or change repository policy.

scope_condition: Required direct-merge state handling and a Needs attention limitation for queue-required repositories. GitHub queue flows and auto-merge remain excluded.
integration_notes: Implement and verify in the initial owning phase; repeat applicable behavior with actual evidence on each later released platform.
requirement_text: The first release supports ordinary permitted direct merges and explicitly excludes GitHub merge-queue enqueue, management, and withdrawal flows. GitHub auto-merge is optional future scope. Distinguish a merge waiting in the local Outbox, a request that may have reached or been accepted by GitHub, and a confirmed merged PR; reconcile uncertain or accepted-but-unconfirmed results before claiming success or retrying. If fresh preflight or a server rejection reveals that the repository requires a GitHub merge queue, retain the submitted intent as Needs attention with a clear unsupported-capability reason and a link to the PR when useful. Do not enqueue it remotely, enable auto-merge, bypass a rule, or change policy. Local cancellation stops eligible local attempts and never implies that a remote merge was undone.

requirement_text: If the intended head changed, permissions or policy no longer permit the action, or current validation conflicts with queued intent, retain the action as Needs attention, preserve the review context, and require a fresh user decision after updating the view. Do not silently retry against a different head. A safe retry of the same intent after temporary transport failure or throttling is automatic under OUTBOX-04/05; an uncertain outcome is reconciled before another attempt.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

requirement_text: Route every explicit remote mutation through a durable SQLite outbox before sending, online as well as offline. Commit a stable operation ID, immutable submitted payload/version, original account and target identities, base values or commit revision, dependency references, draft snapshot, and locally pending projection atomically. Acknowledging Queued requires a successful durable commit; if storage is unavailable or full, keep the editor recoverable and clearly report that the action was not queued. Draft autosave does not authorize dispatch. The explicit action submission is authorization for its automatic later execution, without a routine second confirmation on reconnect.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Durable schema and operation/comment/review step identities in 02; offline UI foundation in 04; full lifecycle, replay, dependencies and step receipts across writers in 07-09.
requirement_text: Use a recoverable operation lifecycle: Queued (including waiting for connection, dependency, pause or retry time), Validating (fresh read/preflight), Sending (a mutation may reach GitHub), Outcome unknown (automatic reconciliation), Waiting for GitHub (accepted asynchronous work), Needs attention (blocked by auth, conflict, unsupported capability or permanent validation failure), Confirmed, and Cancelled. Store a machine-readable reason independently of the state. Unsubmitted Draft is not an outbox entry. Confirmed and Cancelled are terminal only when justified by evidence; an ambiguous or remotely pending action remains inspectable. Exhausted transient retries wait in Queued and resume automatically when eligible.
evidence: ../reports/sprint-02.md Claim, cancel, recover and reconcile after an uncertain send. Writer integration follows in Sprints 07–09.

requirement_text: Provide an Outbox/Pending actions panel that works offline. Show all unresolved submitted actions for the active account, with type, repository, existing target item/comment/thread, payload preview, intended revision/method, state and reason, dependencies, creation/attempt times, and next eligible attempt. Support filters, opening the originating item, individual cancellation, Pause/Resume queued actions, and Retry now when safe. Explain any unavailable control. Pending counts and row states update across panes; confirmed/cancelled history remains inspectable under a documented retention policy. Returning cancelled content to a draft is supported; deleting drafts is separate.

requirement_text: Automatically validate and dispatch eligible submitted actions after reconnection, application restart/wake, dependency completion, authorization repair under the same user, or expiry of a retry delay. Apply bounded exponential backoff with jitter, mutation pacing, shared API budgets, and relevant server headers. Off-hours read schedules and notification quiet hours do not delay already submitted actions. Respect Pause queued actions and Work offline. Definitely unapplied temporary failures remain queued; unrecoverable or content conflicts require attention; uncertain mutation outcomes follow OUTBOX-05. Only the running application/tray can dispatch. [S11] [S12]

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

requirement_text: Prevent duplicate local submission with stable operation IDs, transactional claims, and per-attempt evidence; do not assume this creates server idempotency. For a connection loss, timeout, crash, or ambiguous server error after dispatch, preserve Outcome unknown and reconcile before another mutation. Automatically retry only if reliable evidence shows no remote effect, or verified endpoint idempotency makes it safe. Persist known remote object/operation IDs and confirm through server state where possible. Matching body text or a brief absence from a list is not proof. If still unresolved, retain the action for attention rather than silently replaying or marking success. No unconditional exactly-once delivery guarantee is made.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform
integration_notes: Durable schema and operation/comment/review step identities in 02; offline UI foundation in 04; full lifecycle, replay, dependencies and step receipts across writers in 07-09.
requirement_text: Preserve dependency order for related supported operations while allowing unrelated eligible work to progress under the shared budget. Retain stable local operation/draft identities and record confirmed server identities for comment, review, and thread steps where a later supported operation requires them. Preserve review/thread sequencing and meaningful per-target edit order, including proven predecessor results in later preflight comparisons. Persist step identities and receipts for multi-request workflows; resume eligible unfinished steps rather than repeating completed steps. Show partially applied remote effects explicitly. When a predecessor is cancelled, rejected, or uncertain, hold dependent actions with a clear reason; never guess a remote target or drop descendants silently. Cancelling a parent must show its dependent impact, and users may inspect/cancel each remaining dependent. New-issue placeholders, local issue creation IDs, and create-issue dependency chains are not part of this contract.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

requirement_text: Cancellation of an unsent queued or validating action MUST durably win against dispatch through an atomic state transition checked immediately before the mutation is sent. If cancellation wins, no request for that operation may later be sent, including after restart. If dispatch has already won, show Cancellation requested/May already be sent, stop further mutation attempts, and continue permitted read-only reconciliation. Cancelling an HTTP task is not proof GitHub did nothing. Do not claim remote rollback: a confirmed comment remains a comment and a remotely completed merge remains merged. GitHub merge-queue withdrawal is outside first-release scope. Keep original text, dispatch evidence, and dependent actions recoverable even if sign-out delays reconciliation.

integration_notes: Storage/dispatcher contracts precede actual issue/comment replay in 07; finish uncertain-outcome, cancellation and current-intent validation for reviews and merges by 09.
requirement_text: Freshly validate the original target, permission, edit base values, review anchors, intended commit, merge method, and applicable policy immediately before mutation dispatch. Automatically execute unchanged valid intent without routine reconfirmation. A conflicting remote edit, changed reviewed/merge head, missing target, or changed permission moves the action to Needs attention. Never silently rebase a queued edit, re-anchor a review, approve a new revision, substitute a merge head, or change the chosen merge method. Show the current-versus-intended context so the user can correct or cancel it. Live server enforcement remains authoritative. [S09] [S10]

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

requirement_text: Bind each action permanently to the original host, user/account context, repository/resource identity, and credential owner scope; resolve credentials by protected reference at dispatch, never from a stored token in the payload. Switching users pauses the inactive account's work and isolates its queue contents. Reauthorization may resume the original user's eligible work; another user cannot inherit it. Removing a repository selection preserves its pending work and marks it paused for scope review instead of deleting or secretly sending it. Confirmed locator changes use verified identity and preserve the queue's stable local target.

requirement_text: Treat unresolved outbox operations, payloads, cancellation flags, dependency mappings, base snapshots, anchors, and remote reconciliation evidence as durable user data. Protect them from cache eviction, repair resets, account sign-out, and migration. Recover interrupted claims conservatively after a crash; an interrupted Sending state becomes Outcome unknown unless evidence proves it was never dispatched. Reconcile a successful remote write whose local completion transaction failed. Pending actions have no silent age expiry. Bound and virtualize the outbox UI, redact routine diagnostics, and preserve essential local content until completion/cancellation and any dependent work are settled.

Detect corruption or incompatible schema versions without silently resetting user work. Preserve operation identity, cancellation decisions, and reconciliation evidence across migration and recovery.

requirement_text: Credential switching must isolate private cached data, drafts, and queued actions. Bind each action to its original GitHub user/account access context and credential owner scope. Pause dispatch for inactive identities, signed-out profiles, or known revoked access; resume eligible work under the same verified identity after PAT repair and subject to persisted controls. Replace credentials for the same user without recreating the account, item identities, cache, outbox, or synchronization baselines. Never reroute queued work through another signed-in user. Failed authorization and explicit sign-out preserve local content under AUTH-11; a signed-out local profile remains readable without exposing it through another active account.

requirement_text: Store the visible GitHub number separately from the local primary key and API object IDs. GitHub issues and PRs use the same increasing number sequence within a repository: an issue numbered 41 can be followed by PR 42 and issue 43. There cannot be two distinct items consisting of issue 42 and PR 42 in that repository. Enforce UNIQUE(repository_id, number), without kind in that constraint. Here repository_id identifies a local repository record already scoped to host and account access context. The same number in a different repository or account context must not collide. [S27]

requirement_text: Use an items table for shared fields and a pull_request_details table whose item_id is both its primary key and a foreign key to items. Only confirmed PR items may have this extension. The item kind distinguishes an ordinary issue from a PR once classified. PR summaries may exist before PR details are fetched; a navigation placeholder may remain unclassified until metadata arrives. Track missing detail separately from known false or null values. Keep PR merge state and source references in the extension, and derive the displayed merged state from confirmed PR data. A common closed-state update must not erase known merge information.

requirement_text: Issue endpoints can return PRs, identified by their pull_request property. For that representation, the REST id is an issue ID; the pull-request endpoint supplies the separate PR ID. Store these in distinct typed fields or identity mappings and retain node IDs as opaque provider identifiers. If PR data arrives first, its issue-endpoint ID may remain unknown until fetched. Upsert both representations to the same item using the scoped repository number and verified provider identities. Resolve concurrent ingestion transactionally. Distinguish absent fields from explicit nulls and reject stale overwrites using applicable revision or freshness evidence. Never substitute one ID for the other, create a duplicate row for the second representation, downgrade a known PR because a partial payload omits its marker, or mark unrelated resource families complete. [S28]

Share common labels, assignees, search, drafts, and workspace references through the item identity. requirement_text: Verify artifact integrity and publisher authenticity before execution or installation using the platform's appropriate signing/trust mechanism or a verified signed release manifest with an established trust root. A checksum alone establishes integrity, not publisher authenticity. Download over authenticated transport, validate the selected version/manifest/artifact relationship, fail closed on mismatch or failed verification, and clean up failed staging files. Do not require weakening OS security, disabling certificate checks, execution-policy bypass, or unauthenticated remote-script execution. The documented short command flow must preserve this trust chain.

integration_notes: Storage backup/migration and durable operation invariants begin in 02; real all-state installed upgrades close in 12, then repeat per later platform.
requirement_text: Stage and verify an update before replacing the installed binary. Handle a running instance and file locks safely, prevent simultaneous migration/Outbox dispatch during replacement, and preserve SQLite data, drafts, tabs/layout, settings, offline pins, credential references/protected tokens, sync checkpoints, baselines, and pending-action identities/receipts. Back up user data before risky migrations, and recover from interrupted install/update without falsely confirming actions or losing local work. Roll back binaries only when schema compatibility is safe; do not blindly restore an old Outbox snapshot that could replay already applied mutations. Explain recovery if migration cannot safely continue.

requirement_text: Rerunning the same install command MUST detect an installed matching version and finish successfully without duplicating shortcuts, startup entries, instances, data directories or credentials. Support a documented stable channel and explicit version selection; upgrades preserve stable app identity and state. Reject unsafe downgrades or schema incompatibility with clear recovery guidance. Startup-on-login remains opt-in; installation must not silently activate background networking or override offline/pause settings.

scope_condition: Required for each applicable released platform

requirement_text: Failures MUST provide a short actionable explanation, a nonzero exit code when applicable, and a safe rerun path without asking users to compile or inspect developer logs for routine problems. Test denied permissions, blocked downloads, insufficient disk space, interrupted downloads, signature/hash failure, incompatible OS/architecture, missing prerequisite, and running-app locks. Do not request an application PAT for a public installer or expose credentials in commands/logs. If a chosen private release distribution requires separate download authorization, document that boundary without reusing the app's GitHub PAT implicitly.

requirement_text: Provide a documented uninstall path using native platform conventions or an installed uninstaller. Uninstall removes app binaries and registrations while preserving local user data by default; removing data or protected credentials is an explicit separate choice with pending-work consequences shown. Reinstall must recover the retained profile, workspace and progress instead of forcing a full archive. Respect the already specified distinction between ordinary exit, explicit sign-out and cache deletion.

No release repository, URL or binary is available in this specification package: all illustrative commands are labeled templates until replaced with actual published endpoints and tested. Record clean-machine install, rerun, upgrade with seeded drafts/Outbox, failure recovery and uninstall/reinstall evidence on each claimed platform. A script file, placeholder URL or successful source build is not completed installer acceptance. [S35]

requirement_text: Implement a documented development test runner and relevant tests in every sprint, not only at release. The required command contract is cargo xtask test unit; cargo xtask test integration; cargo xtask test ui; cargo xtask test e2e --suite smoke or --suite full; cargo xtask test install --artifact <path>; and cargo xtask test live --repo OWNER/REPO with an explicit --allow-live-writes opt-in for approved mutations. Implement these commands or a documented equivalent wrapper before claiming their gates passed. They are planned commands, not tools already provided by this requirements ZIP. Each command returns a meaningful exit status, reports selected/skipped/blocked tests and environment, and writes machine-readable results plus concise logs. End users install prebuilt binaries and need none of this development tooling.

Cover pagination/resumption, SSO/permissions/partial data, rate limits, cache publication, persisted checkpoints, signed-out identity holds, Outbox claiming/reconciliation, and upgrade cleanup protection. Verify production interfaces with deterministic simulated remote responses and OS adapter contract tests; use real protected-store/notification integration checks on the applicable native host. requirement_text: End-to-end tests MUST launch and drive the actual native application process through its user-visible controls using supported native automation/accessibility/input, with real local persistence and the implemented HTTP adapter connected to a deterministic test server where appropriate. Start with launch/focus/quit smoke coverage in Sprint 01 and expand to cache-first reading, tab/context switching, offline drafts, queued submissions/cancellation/reconnect, review/merge revision guards, notifications and restoration as those features arrive. Screenshots, GPUI in-process UI tests, callbacks, domain function calls, or a web browser test are not substitutes for native-process E2E. Keep GPUI UI integration tests as an additional layer. Distinguish simulator/test-build native E2E from smoke and release checks of the exact installed published package; the former does not prove packaging, release feature flags or publisher trust. A native automation gap is a visible blocked gate, not a reason to relabel a unit test E2E; record reproducible manual evidence for any inherently manual OS prompt and automate the remaining journey.
